notes: Traditional Chinese proper-noun glossary for Betrayal at Krondor. No official Chinese translation exists for this game or its novelization (Krondor: The Betrayal) -- the only confirmed official term is Pug/帕格, from the Taiwan-published translation of the original Riftwar Saga novels (Gaea Books/Sharp Point), which this game is a spin-off of. Everything else here is an original, internally-consistent transliteration/translation, informed by that confirmed term's style. Consult this file before translating any DDX entry that names a person, place, faction, or notable object; add new terms here the first time they appear, don't improvise a fresh rendering per-entry.

Derogatory epithet Patrus uses for moredhel/goblin forces collectively during the goblin bridge-toll negotiation (DIAL_Z22).
Midwinter's Festival gift-giving folk figure (a Santa Claus analogue) Owyn compares himself to while surprising Lurough with a wine cask (DIAL_Z22).
Signature name on a handwritten closure notice tacked to the Candlemaker's Grin tavern door (established 燭匠的笑臉), identified as its proprietor (DIAL_Z22#51); not directly encountered, note-only.
James's informant/contact in the Krondor sewers, tells Owyn where James went; part of the palace-escape scene at the start of the Sar-Sargoth rescue chapter (DIAL_Z23).
Krondor's royal cavalry/guard unit that impostor Nighthawks hope to lure into the sewers as a pretext to raid the Mockers (DIAL_Z23).

Full name given for Tomas, Lord of Elvandar (established 托馬斯), when Owyn reads about him in one of Pug's journals at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z23#102). Use plain 托馬斯 elsewhere as already established; this full form is only for this specific reference.

Queen of the eledhel elves of Elvandar (Tomas's wife in Riftwar Saga canon); Gorath cites her kin as ancient enemies of the moredhel when explaining why Elvandar will not welcome him (DIAL_Z23#102); not directly encountered.
Kingdom town, location of a 'Roots 'N Herbs' shop cited as a well-run business example in a trading-strategy book excerpt at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z23#91).
Kingdom town, location of an 'Arms of Dala' shop cited in the same Vaults of Sarth trading-strategy excerpt (DIAL_Z23#91).
Krondor priest/scholar credited with developing a new Silverthorn (established 銀刺) anti-venom, author of the book excerpt read at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z23#99); not directly encountered.
Northlands shore where Silverthorn poison is now mass-harvested, per Father Nathan's book (DIAL_Z23#99).
Site scholars speculate gives Silverthorn its lethality via soil nutrients, per Father Nathan's book (DIAL_Z23#99).
Site of an early battle against goblins where the 'Invitation' spell was first used by Althafain (established 阿爾薩芬), per a soldier's tactics book at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z23#106).
A spell originally dismissed as a magicians' prank, used by Althafain to lure a band of the Dark Brothers (established 黑暗兄弟) into a trap at the battle of Carse (DIAL_Z23#106).
Location/army whose military company a healer travelled with, per a healer's journal read at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z23#96); not otherwise described.
Traveling healer near LaMut who sells cures for 25 sovereigns; a tavern patron suspects she's colluding with Orno the Pale to spread and then 'cure' a fake plague (DIAL_Z31).
Man reportedly stricken with an unknown contagion, suspected of colluding with Michele the Healer (DIAL_Z31); render "the Pale" as a bracketed epithet before the name.
Small-time pickpocket/thief who offers to teach lockpicking after being caught red-handed (DIAL_Z31).
Fencing instructor who offers sword lessons for 75 sovereigns; has two young students including Mitch (DIAL_Z31).
Old man who tends a warded healing well near his house, claims not to be a magician despite carving magic symbols (DIAL_Z31).
River fisherman selling dried trout, shovels, and torches (DIAL_Z31).
Very tall man in Wolfram (established 沃夫拉姆), doubles as the town's hangman (DIAL_Z31).
Sorcerer who wagers his Lightning Staff (established 雷霆杖) on a three-question riddle game, tricked by Owyn's party (DIAL_Z31).
Crippled moredhel veteran, lamed in a fortress assault while following Murmandamus, now unable to fight (DIAL_Z31).
Gorath's late friend, mentioned in a fond memory about a well's construction; left to follow Murmandamus and never returned (DIAL_Z31).
Dark-skinned elf encountered in an Elvandar treehouse, points the party toward Warleader Tomas (DIAL_Z31).
Tall elf shopkeeper in an Elvandar treehouse shop, boasts of Warleader Tomas as a regular customer (DIAL_Z31).
Former scout for King Lyam in Rillanon, hired by the elves as a mercenary guard near Elvandar (DIAL_Z31).
Slight, balding historian researching the Valheru and the Sethanon cataclysm, met near Elvandar (DIAL_Z31).
Name signed on tax-record notes found in a moredhel dwelling near Sar-Sargoth (DIAL_Z31); not directly encountered.
Farmer suspected of setting up an ambush in his own barn near Highcastle (DIAL_Z31); not directly encountered on-screen.
Goblin chief who sends goblins to raid a moredhel illusionist's spellbooks near Northwarden (DIAL_Z31); not directly encountered.
Elderly former Swordmaster (established 劍術大師) of Highcastle, regales the party with old war stories (DIAL_Z31).

Member of a mercenary raiding party near Dencamp on the Teeth, killed by a troll after his magic-scroll countermeasure worked on goblins but not trolls (DIAL_Z31); not directly encountered, deceased before the party arrives.
Hunter/farmer near Highcastle who found three strange inscribed chests while out hunting (DIAL_Z31); not directly encountered, referenced by his wife.

Established family surname (see Flendel Halfgate and Thea, both already listed). DIAL_Z31 introduces several more siblings living separately near Highcastle: a widow (哈夫蓋特寡婦, unnamed), Gena (吉娜) and her sister Andrea (安德麗雅) who trade a tuning fork for leather leggings, Sara (莎拉) who trades grain for leather leggings, and Larissa (拉莉莎) whose barn door the party frees and who gifts a tuning fork/shell/herb pack in thanks. Keep the shared surname consistent across all of them.

entries.translation: 世界之齒山下的丹肯營地
entries.notes: A mercenary camp at the foot of the Teeth of the World (established 世界之齒), where a raiding party is recruiting for a Northlands treasure hunt using changing passwords (DIAL_Z31). Shorten to 丹肯營地 after first mention in a scene.
Small town with a pottery shop, a general store called 'Guds', and an inn called 'The Royal Bed' (DIAL_Z31).
Place a wounded dwarf near Elvandar says he travelled from (DIAL_Z31); not otherwise described.
A large stone slab/monument near Sar-Sargoth that reacts to an emerald placed in its notch, triggering a dramatic energy burst (DIAL_Z31).
An elven-marked magical well near Elvandar; mixing its water with Fadamor's Formula (established 法達莫爾秘方) permanently increases strength (DIAL_Z31).
Winning call in a dwarven dice game played near Elvandar -- shouted by whoever grabs the other player's stone first after a matching "double dragon" roll (DIAL_Z31).
A losing/void roll outcome in the dwarven dice game (established alongside Klapka, DIAL_Z31); two "vookas" in a row lose to a single dragon roll.

Tsurani innkeeper of the Blue Wheel Inn (established 藍輪客棧) in LaMut; a former Patrol Leader of House Shinzawai under Earl Kasumi, stranded in Midkemia since the Rift War, teaches combat lessons (DIAL_Z20).
Tsurani noble house Sumani served under Earl Kasumi (DIAL_Z20).
Tsurani noble house in conflict with House Acoma (established 阿科瑪家) over succession, temporarily halting rift-gate transport (DIAL_Z20).
Tsurani death god, the punchline deity of a nonsensical Tsurani joke Sumani tells (DIAL_Z20).
A brand/type of unpickable lock commonly found on abandoned houses near LaMut (DIAL_Z20).
Talkative dwarf associated with the LaMut garrison, known for haggling skill and tall tales (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen in this chapter.
Innkeeper/barkeep at Malac's Cross (established 馬拉克十字鎮) and enthusiastic chess gambler, wagers emeralds; possibly a relative of Lysle Rigger (DIAL_Z20).
Krondor sewer contact who confirms the Upright Man's (established 正直人) suspicion that the Crawler (established 爬行者) is not Jocko Radburn (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
Historical corrupt captain of the watch who besieged Krondor alongside Guy du Bas-Tyra (established 居伊．杜．巴斯泰拉) in James's youth; referenced only in backstory (DIAL_Z20).

Swordmaster and pokiir (established 波基爾) player at The Stranger Tavern (established 陌生人酒館) in Eggley; full Quegian name Devonius. Former mercenary who served the Dauphiness of Queg, sank King Lebeus's flagship with Spitzer, then went independent (DIAL_Z20). Already referenced as a rumor source in DIAL_Z13.
Devon's old comrade-in-arms, boarded the warship Storm's Master with him against King Lebeus's flagship; last seen in Tanneurs (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
The Dauphiness of Queg's war galley Devon and Spitzer used to sink King Lebeus's flagship (DIAL_Z20).
King of Queg, referenced as a feared, punitive ruler (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Naddur's brother, a source of news about moredhel pressing the borders near Moraelin (established 莫拉埃林) (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Epithet of a prowler/lockpick who moved into Hawk's Hollow (established 鷹谷), no lock in town he hasn't bypassed (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered, kept as a literal epithet like "the Upright Man".
Old woman who left a keg of Keshian ale behind at a tavern near Sarth (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
Monk at an abbey near Malac's Cross/Queen's Row, studying Quegian civil codes, knowledgeable about spellcasting (DIAL_Z20); distinct from Brother Marc and Brother Anthony at Sarth.
Monk at the same abbey as Brother Dominic, tracks weather predictions (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.

The greatest emerald mine the dwarves ever delved, in caverns beneath Sarth partly underlying the Abbey of Ishap; the region above is called Bourgalan (established Keshian name, matches "Quegian Fever" being properly called "Bourgalan Fever" per a testy dwarf). Now held by Mejakaar Blackpatch's successors/the Brothers of Ishap (DIAL_Z20).

Deceased former lord who moved into the keep built over one entrance to Mac Bourgalan Dok, prompting the dwarves to cede the caverns; long dead by the time of DIAL_Z20, now nominally held by the Brothers of Ishap.
Macros the Black's (established 黑袍馬克羅斯) home on Sorcerer's Isle (established 法師之島), referenced in legends held at the Vaults of Sarth (DIAL_Z20).
Island home of Macros the Black, site of the Villa Beata (DIAL_Z20).
Inn recommended near Questor's View (established 尋道崖) (DIAL_Z20).
Old inn recommended near Sarth (DIAL_Z20).

Son of Warleader Tomas (established 托馬斯) and Queen Aglaranna (established 亞葛拉蘭娜王后); takes command of Elvandar's border patrols after Tomas is poisoned, teaches Owyn elven stealth and offers to teach Gorath crossbow use, addressing him as "our cousin" (moredhel and eledhel being kin) (DIAL_Z20).

One of Queen Aglaranna's elven Spellweavers (established 織法者) at Elvandar, helps contain wildfires and devises countermeasures against moredhel-controlled wyverns (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
Mountain marking the entrance to a subterranean ancient ruin (a Valheru site) leading toward the heart of Elvandar (DIAL_Z20).
Deceased predecessor as Huntsmaster of Carse, before Duke Martin's recommendation brought in the current Huntsmaster (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Duke of Crydee (established 克萊迪) who took in Kulgan (established 庫爾根) and Pug in his duchy, cited by Duke Martin as the wisdom behind keeping magicians on staff at Northwarden (DIAL_Z20).
Admiral of the Western Fleet, a mutual acquaintance of James and Duke Martin, jokingly compared to Patrus (established) for brashness (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
Leads a counter-attack force stationed at Sethanon; Delekhan's forces know they must get past his men (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
A ship, subject of an old joke Prince Arutha used to tell his sister Carline about being roped to its mainmast for target practice (DIAL_Z20).
Prince Arutha's sister, referenced only in an old joke about Krondor's Glory (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Soldier quartered at Northwarden, wrote a love letter to a girl named Thea intercepted (harmlessly) during James's guard-duty test of the castle's security (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
James and Locklear's former Master of Ceremonies from their days running errands/billets in Krondor, referenced fondly in passing (DIAL_Z20/Z31).
Helps care for the children at the Corvalis Cavall Keep household during the wartime crisis (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.

Count Corvalis's solicitor, one of Ugyne's two suitors (neither approved of by her father); lives near Cavall Keep with his daughter Ami. Has a minor claim to nobility via a brother who is an Earl (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Myron's daughter (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.

entries.translation: 納馮．杜桑多／內維爾．科瓦利斯
entries.notes: MAJOR REVEAL (DIAL_Z20): Navon du Sandau, Ugyne's suitor (previously listed only as "linked to the impostor Nighthawks"), is in fact her brother Neville Corvalis, believed dead in a childhood wine-cellar collapse. Count Corvalis (established 科瓦利斯伯爵) discovered Neville was illegitimate and staged the "accident" to remove him from the succession; Neville survived, was taken in by Nighthawks fleeing Prince Arutha, discovered a mind-reading spyglass, and eventually became the Nighthawks' own leader -- using the alias Navon du Sandau (borrowing the name of the drunken workman blamed for the cellar collapse) to insinuate himself back into the family and court his own sister without her knowledge. Defeated and interrogated by James/Jimmy the Hand in this chapter. Keep both names distinct depending on context: characters who know only the cover story call him Navon; the reveal itself uses Neville.

A restless ghost's true grave-occupant; an oracle instructs the party to recover his hand from Lyton (established 萊頓) and rebury it in Sethanon's honored-dead ground to end a haunting (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
Cook at the Krondor palace kitchens, currently idle since Prince Arutha has been dining privately; Katala fetches pre-made rations from him (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered on-screen.
Buyer of Stardock Academy magical exports, lives north of Romney (DIAL_Z20); not directly encountered.
An unofficial shop at the Abbey of Ishap at Sarth trading on the Stardock Academy's name, though it has no real ties to the Academy (DIAL_Z20).
Leader of the kobolds/gnomes near Mac Mordain Cadal, periodically leads holy quests to find their lost dragon-god, per a dwarf's account (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Dwarven term for the small dragon-worshipping creatures that humans call gnomes; both terms refer to the same race (DIAL_Z30).
Human term for the creatures dwarves call kobolds (科博德); a dwarf explains "your folk call them gnomes" (DIAL_Z30). Distinct from any unrelated uses of "gnome" elsewhere.
A passage within the Prince's sewers of Krondor guarded by a young Mockers lookout who answers to the Upright Man (DIAL_Z30).
A Mockers guild rank/lieutenant title, the sewer gatekeepers answer to him and he in turn answers to the Upright Man (DIAL_Z30).
Mentioned in passing by Devon as one of the few people still in Eggley besides himself (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.

Eggley's local ritual: elders draw lots for who becomes "The Stranger", who hands out fake coins (nimptos, 尼普托) and circles the town swinging hemp rope the next morning to signal Killian's blessing (DIAL_Z30, Devon's story).
Fake sovereign coins handed out during Eggley's Festival of the Stranger ritual (DIAL_Z30).

Minstrel forcibly stationed at Northwarden by Baron Gabot (established 加博特男爵) as punishment for a romantic scandal; gives music lessons for a fee and requests a bowstring for lute resin (DIAL_Z30). Directly encountered on-screen.

Ancient dragon-skinned prophetic being consulted by Pug near Malac's Cross; last of the Aal race, older than dwarves, elves, dragons, and the Valheru (DIAL_Z30). Vulnerable to Makala's Valheru amulet, which can compel her dragon-flesh body even though he cannot control her mind.
Epithet "Master of Dragons" -> 群龍之主; ancient Valheru credited with crafting the amulet Makala uses against the Oracle of the Aal (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Paired with Mythar (麥薩) in the Oracle of the Aal's cryptic prophecy to Owyn about a future "critical juncture"; meaning left deliberately unexplained in-story (DIAL_Z30).
Paired with Rythar (萊薩) in the Oracle of the Aal's cryptic prophecy to Owyn about a future "critical juncture"; meaning left deliberately unexplained in-story (DIAL_Z30).
Street/district in Malac's Cross where Ivan Skaald's tavern and a famous chess match take place (DIAL_Z30).
Duke Martin's wife, referenced in passing by Martin as a joking reason Owyn might be hunting rabbits for a ducal stew (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.

Keshian noble/envoy angered after a Kingdom ship mistakenly sank an Imperial Keshian frigate, mentioned by Duke Martin as the reason King Lyam can't spare attention for Northwarden's battle (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
One of the Duchess (of Yabon)'s daughters, mentioned by Squire Phillip as "the prettiest" at a party (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
One of the Duchess (of Yabon)'s daughters, described by Squire Phillip as fickle like her mother and interested in marrying a conDoin (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
A moredhel military company that fell back from Northwarden with the Tsurani rift machine; Duke Martin infiltrated it disguised as a mercenary (DIAL_Z30).
Monster Prince Calin credits the party with slaying near an Elvandar border checkpoint (DIAL_Z30 random encounter callback).
Military title used before Tomas's name ("Warleader Tomas"), Elvandar's supreme military commander (established from earlier chapters, formalized here).
Formal name of the Tsurani (established 圖蘭尼) homeland empire on the other side of the rift, mentioned by Sumani at the Blue Wheel Inn (DIAL_Z30).
A Tsurani beverage served at Sumani's Blue Wheel Inn in LaMut (DIAL_Z30).
A Tsurani deity Sumani invokes as a farewell blessing ("May Chochoan watch over you") at the Blue Wheel Inn (DIAL_Z30).
Tsurani political intrigue/assassination custom Sumani hopes never becomes commonplace in Midkemia (DIAL_Z30); referenced but not detailed on-screen.
Krondor tavern where Nivek, the West Region treasurer (established 尼維克), can be found drinking (DIAL_Z30).
Inn near Sethanon run by/associated with Nia (established 妮雅); mentioned by McCannur and Nivek (DIAL_Z30).
Woman at the Six Toe inn (六趾客棧) near Sethanon; Nivek's drunken ramblings reveal she was frightened by Max Feeber digging in a graveyard near Sethanon (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered on-screen.

Full name of Jared (established 賈瑞德, the restless ghost from DIAL_Z20's haunting subplot); Nivek's drunken story reveals he refused to sell land near Sethanon to Max Feeber (established 麥克斯．費伯) (DIAL_Z30).
Lysle Rigger's (established 萊斯爾．瑞格) birthplace, mentioned when he explains he is not James's brother (DIAL_Z30). Transliterated distinctly from Tsurani (established 圖蘭尼) to avoid visual confusion.

Man in Lyton (established 萊頓) who bought the skeletal "glory hand" from Lysle Rigger, later killed by the Crawler's men investigating who was training thieves in magic (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Romney craft guild allied with the Glazer's Guild (established 玻璃匠公會) against the Riverpullers in the guild war (DIAL_Z30).
Romney craft guild whose head the Duke of Romney needs at the negotiating table to end the guild war (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
River crossing at Romney where the labor guilds (north bank) and craft guilds (south bank) are deadlocked during the guild war (DIAL_Z30).
Historical Kingdom king proverbial for madness, invoked by Mitchel Waylander (established 米契爾．韋蘭德) as a comparison ("mad as old King Rodric") (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
An assassin's tool associated with the Nighthawks (established 夜鷹會), found on murdered Bas-Tyra soldiers' bodies alongside a brass spyglass (DIAL_Z30).

A boy's late master/caretaker in Romney; told the boy before dying that "the Collectors" (established 收容人) would come take him somewhere nice, a euphemism the boy repeats not understanding it means death (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.

An orphaned tavern boy's euphemism (taught to him by his late master Carolus, established 卡羅魯斯) for whoever/whatever comes to take dead or dying people to a peaceful place; distinct from the unrelated Eggley "Collector" debt-collector character (established 收帳人) -- do not merge the two (DIAL_Z30).
Non-poisonous herb that induces excessive thirst when mixed into ale, used to get the Bas-Tyra soldiers drunk before the Nighthawks' ambush (DIAL_Z30).
Orphaned boy working at the Black Sheep Tavern (established 黑羊酒館) in Romney; present when Nighthawks massacred the King's men there, gives the party key eyewitness details (DIAL_Z30).
Establishment in Silden that sent wine to the Bas-Tyra soldiers at the Black Sheep Tavern shortly before the Nighthawk massacre (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Inn near Silden where Abuk (established 阿布克) plans to wait for his delayed trader friend (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Tavern in Silden; a raven nailed to its doorpost signals the Crawler (established 爬行者) has convened his assistants and strangers should leave town (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
A famously unpickable brand/type of lock, referenced by a locksmith character near Silden (DIAL_Z30).
Abuk's (established 阿布克) lockpicking master, taught him for five years at Mount Ashunta (established 阿舜塔山) (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Keshian mountain where Abuk (established 阿布克) trained under his master Caliphad (established 卡里法德) (DIAL_Z30).
Abuk's (established 阿布克) father, named in his formal self-introduction (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Runs the Anchorhead Tavern (established 錨首酒館) in Silden; earlier established as the man Abuk (established 阿布克) sold the brass spyglass to; directly encountered on-screen selling rations (DIAL_Z30).

A boat that sometimes harbors in Silden; a dead Nighthawk's ticket for passage to Krondor on it was found by Abuk (established 阿布克) (DIAL_Z30). Deliberately echoes "the Crawler" (established 爬行者) in the source text -- keep the echo in translation, don't disambiguate it away.

Restless water spirits ("sisters of Eliaem", established 伊萊亞姆) that linger near rivers and resist being sent to Lims-Kragma's (established 林斯克拉格瑪) halls; Beyla (established 貝拉) tasks the party with finding and laying them to rest (DIAL_Z30).
Ship that ferries the party to and from Beyla's (established 貝拉) island temple of Eortis (established 埃奧提斯), sailing out of Silden (DIAL_Z30).

Woman hiding from the Mockers in the Krondor sewers, secretly working against the Crawler (established 爬行者) from within; sends the party to find the Idol of Lassur (established 拉蘇爾神像), knowing it will kill the Crawler within a month of him claiming it (DIAL_Z30).

Bronze statue rumored to grant its owner power over life; actually belongs to Lassur (established 拉蘇爾), an Isalani name for the death goddess Lims-Kragma (established 林斯克拉格瑪) -- any mortal who claims it dies within a month (DIAL_Z30).
River an underground stream beneath Venutrier's (established 維努特里爾) mines flows into, part of Gorath and Obkhar's (established 奧布卡) escape route (DIAL_Z30).
A southern culture/language referenced as the source of "Lassur" (established 拉蘇爾), an alternate name for Lims-Kragma (established 林斯克拉格瑪) (DIAL_Z30).

A foreign (to Obkhar/moredhel) word for a magic item that can collapse a Tsurani rift gate when thrown into its maelstrom; Obkhar killed a gate-guarding magician to obtain one and used it, then seeks another (DIAL_Z30).
Kingdom officer commanding the garrison at Inclindel Pass (established 因克林德爾山口); recurs across multiple chapters reporting on whether the pass is open (DIAL_Z30).

Hardy hillmen people from the Northlands, referenced as fleeing south to Yabon (established 亞邦) during an especially severe winter -- notable because they normally never seek refuge in towns (DIAL_Z30).
Mountain pass near Northwarden (established 北衛城), suggested by Lieutenant Finn (established 芬恩中尉) as an alternate route when the Inclindel is blocked (DIAL_Z30).
Old man whose house near the graveyard is where Max Feeber (established 麥克斯．費伯) thinks he dropped the skeletal hand he dug up (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Petrumh's (established 佩特魯姆) late husband, whom she believes was killed by elves near Sethanon amid "faerie lights" in the Dimwood (established 幽暗林) (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.

One-eyed dwarf veteran drinking at the Blue Wheel Inn (established 藍輪客棧) in LaMut; rescued Locklear and other refugees from a cellar during the Battle of Sethanon, later reveals Sumani's (established 蘇馬尼) backstory (DIAL_Z30).
Petrumh's (established 佩特魯姆) friend in Darkmoor (established 黑沼鎮), at whose house she plans to stay (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
A Tsurani man's adopted Kingdom name (his original Tsurani name considered unpronounceable), works for Duke Martin in Crydee (established 克萊迪) (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Battle referenced in a tactics-lecture anecdote where student Kyle Fischer publicly debated Guy du Bas-Tyra's (established 居伊．杜．巴斯泰拉) tactics (DIAL_Z30).

Roguish con-man and old acquaintance of Locklear and James; eleven years earlier impersonated the Count of Dorgin's son at Arutha's wedding and was exposed/expelled by James, now works odd jobs/schemes along the border (DIAL_Z30).
Master of Ceremonies who nearly threw Isaac (established 艾薩克) over the palace walls upon discovering his impersonation, mentioned only in Isaac's reminiscence (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Nobleman whose son Isaac (established 艾薩克) once impersonated at Arutha's wedding (DIAL_Z30); not directly encountered.
Mountain near Sarth and the Temple of Sung (established 頌神神殿), landmark on the way to Rowe's (established 羅威) barn (DIAL_Z30).
Temple near Sarth (established 薩斯) used as a landmark on the road south, dedicated to Sung (established 頌神) (DIAL_Z30).

Cave not far from Northwarden containing "pattern stones" (established 命紋石) that geomancers use to foretell a person's future; Tamney (established 坦尼) sends the party to fetch one before deciding whether to return to duty (DIAL_Z30).
Small stones found in the Diviner's Halls (established 占卜者廳堂), used by geomancers to foretell a person's future (DIAL_Z30).
Ship a Nighthawk (identified by a hawk emblem) booked passage on from Silden to Krondor, per Joftaz (established 喬夫塔茲) (DIAL_Z30).
Epithet for Banath (established 巴納斯神), god of luck and thieves, used by Joftaz (established 喬夫塔茲) (DIAL_Z30).
